scientific_goal: Learn a stable and statistically faithful rank-20 0p20 Neural-SDE on the exact 5%-trimmed training population without MC-GMM, using the proven no-extra-history Markov architecture, positive diagonal restoring+damping drift, conditional velocity energy-score training, and staged endpoint mean then variance calibration.
scientific_constraints: Treat the exact checkpoint 5% training-increment trim as the primary target population. Generated trajectories remain untrimmed, but primary energy, POD moments and PSD comparisons use the reference retained by the checkpoint's native-velocity complete-stencil rule; report untrimmed-reference numbers separately.
Tune only on validation repetitions 13 and 14. Test repetitions 15 and 16 remain locked.
All trained candidates start within this study from random initialization or from a checkpoint learned within this study. Existing 0p20 runs are evidence-only seeds and may not initialize training.

Keep the rank-20 shared-POD data, stored 50 Hz high-pass spatial mean, native-lag velocity state, positive diagonal restoring plus damping operators and state-independent diagonal diffusion fixed during the follow-up. The primary new branch replaces the TCN residual with the ordinary Markov MLP residual and uses only the current position plus native-frame velocity state.
The TCN uses 63 dense frames, 64 channels, kernel size 3 and dilations 1,2,4,8,16. It replaces only the nonlinear residual; explicit restoring and damping remain active.

Use the unbiased conditional velocity energy score in target-standardized coordinates, initially with four independent paths per measured start and no self-pairs. Prefer broad initial-condition coverage over a large particle ensemble.

Use batch-level multistep sampling initially for throughput. Distinguish objective quality from stochastic update variance, and permit a matched examples-sampling check if batch-level updates appear noisy.

First establish one-step and energy-only effects. Add endpoint mean matching next; add light variance matching only after diagnosing amplitude or covariance error. Keep their weighted contributions and gradient roles separate.
Changing the maximum energy-score horizon requires a matching particle-count schedule in the same decision. Horizon 20 is the main extension; horizon 50 is allowed only if it remains economical.

Do not attribute a gain solely to energy score when horizon eligibility changes. One-step NLL still uses the retained one-step population independently; compare retained fractions and matched validation diagnostics.

Judge survival, trimmed-reference energy, POD mean and covariance, leading-mode amplitude, PSD, ACF, innovation calibration and one-step conditional statistics separately. A visually good center PSD is not sufficient.

Orthogonality is a late optional ablation after a stable energy-plus-moment candidate exists. Its effect must be demonstrated from actual penalty values and a matched rollout, not assumed from the structured ansatz.
Diffusion architecture is checkpoint-invariant. Never change diffusion type during checkpoint fine-tuning.

The earlier constant full-covariance one-step ablation was negative. One user-authorized fresh follow-up may combine constant full-covariance diffusion with the short TCN15 and energy-score multistep training; do not infer success from the covariance parameterization alone.

Treat temporal receptive field as a fresh-model architecture ablation. Permitted matched TCNs are context 7 with dilations 1,2; context 15 with dilations 1,2,4; context 31 with dilations 1,2,4,8; and the existing context 63 with dilations 1,2,4,8,16. Never change context or dilations during checkpoint fine-tuning.

Use the historical 0p20 no-history MC-GMM recipe as a mechanistic guide: weight 0.1 and horizons 2,4,10,20 produced a faithful long rollout. First test the analogous energy-score recipe on shorter TCNs, then vary one of weight or horizon set at a time. An economical GMM-NLL control is allowed, but it must obey the 45-minute cap and report its active particle schedule.

Do not compare objective values across energy score and GMM NLL as though they shared units. Select weights from rollout amplitude, covariance, PSD and conditional diagnostics, not equality of raw loss magnitudes.

The energy-score and GMM comparison is complete. Do not implement or request a hybrid objective and do not train additional GMM-NLL candidates. The follow-up tests whether removing the TCN lets energy score plus endpoint moments recover the successful Markov-model behavior.

Train fresh no-TCN energy-score anchors before moment calibration. Compare energy-score weights with horizons and all other settings held fixed. Add endpoint mean matching only after a candidate is finite and materially closer in energy/covariance; add variance matching only after mean calibration is shown not to damage stability or PSD.

Endpoint moments are refinement objectives, not safe initializers. Do not train a moments-only model from random initialization. Prefer the historically effective horizons 100,200,500 with 30 or 64 trajectories, and log raw and weighted mean/variance contributions.
Every training subprocess has a hard 2700-second wall-clock limit. Timed-out partial directories are retained and failed, never continued.

One explicitly authorized fresh TCN31 diagnostic may set training trimming to 0% while holding the best TCN31 energy-score configuration fixed. Evaluate it against the untrimmed validation reference first and use consecutive-increment correlation, energy, covariance, stability, and innovation calibration to determine whether long-stencil trimming removed essential reversal and recovery dynamics.

Screen every candidate on 32 independent full-strength stochastic validation paths for 5000 steps. Reject nonfinite paths, peak POD standardized RMS above 10, absolute standardized coordinate above 50, trimmed-reference energy outside [0.4,2.5], or trimmed-reference covariance trace outside [0.4,2.5].
At most one candidate receives an independent 50000-step confirmation. Prefer the simplest economical model whose trimmed-reference energy, covariance and PSD remain good at confirmation.
advisor_guidance: Thirteen trained trials are complete. Do not implement the previously requested hybrid score, and do not run more GMM-NLL or full-diffusion trials. The short-TCN study found context 31 better than context 15, but every energy-score TCN remained overdispersed: the best was context 31, weight 0.03, with trimmed energy 1.691 and covariance trace 1.633. The economical GMM control moved in the opposite direction, energy 0.930 and covariance trace 0.523, with severe mean and PSD errors. Historical successful 0p20 models instead used an ordinary no-extra-history Markov MLP residual. The plain multistep model reached 50000-step untrimmed energy 1.04 and covariance trace 0.991; later endpoint-mean or mean-plus-variance fine-tuning from a stable multistep checkpoint reached trimmed-target energy about 1.09, covariance trace 0.958, POD-mean error 0.049-0.062 and POD-only PSD error 0.384-0.477 decades. Test whether this architecture, rather than MC-GMM itself, explains the success. First run a fresh damped-residual Markov MLP with diagonal diffusion, energy-score horizons 2,4,10,20, four particles, drift-plus-diffusion gradients, learning rate 0.001, batch size 256 and five epochs. Start with weight 0.03 because it was the best TCN weight, then compare 0.01 or 0.1 with everything else fixed if needed. Do not use endpoint moments until one no-TCN energy-score anchor is stable and reasonably close in energy and covariance. Then fine-tune the best anchor with endpoint mean weight around 0.01 at horizons 100,200,500, followed only if supported by variance weight around 0.001. TCN7 is allowed only as a final fallback after the no-TCN branch, not before it. Never exceed 45 minutes per training subprocess and keep test repetitions locked.

seed_runs.hypothesis: Existing one-step 0p20 TCN63 reference with good local sequence modeling but excess trimmed-reference amplitude and poor rollout PSD.
Existing structured non-TCN reference showing useful amplitude control but remaining spatial-mean and spectral mismatch.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Five one-step epochs learn a strong local structured TCN63 model on the exact trimmed 0p20 population and supply a clean parent for generated-history fine-tuning.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Improved local NLL and innovation behavior but excess autonomous amplitude, motivating staged energy-score training.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Energy-score feedback active from random initialization can jointly learn local and closed-loop 0p20 dynamics without a separate one-step stage.
initial_trials.expected_observation: A finite 5000-step rollout with lower trimmed-reference energy and covariance error than the one-step and external TCN references; failure supports staged optimization.
